cards.claim: MUON optimizer can be generalized to use arbitrary polynomial degrees for Newton-Schulz steps, covering both the original fixed quintic and alternative polynomials like Polar Express
cards.conditions: Generalized MUON variant with configurable polynomial coefficients; arbitrary number of NS steps
cards.effect: Not quantified in abstract; theoretical framework only
cards.quote: We propose and study a generalized variant of the MUON optimizer involving an arbitrary number of generalized NS steps with polynomials of possibly arbitrary high degree. The considered optimizer covers MUON with the original NS polynomial as well as MUON combined with the recently proposed Polar Express method as special cases.

cards.claim: MUON convergence is sensitive to mini-batch size—fails to converge for almost every mini-batch size on simple stochastic optimization problems
cards.conditions: Simple class of stochastic optimization problems; mini-batch size variation; infinite gradient step limit
cards.effect: Non-convergence (failure to converge) for almost all mini-batch sizes
cards.quote: For a simple class of stochastic optimization problems (SOPs) we show for almost every mini-batch size that MUON fails to converge to the solution of the SOP as the number of gradient steps converges to infinity.

cards.claim: Error analysis for MUON with generalized NS steps yields convergence rates dependent on both gradient step count and mini-batch size
cards.conditions: Generalized NS steps; quadratic SOPs and ℓ₂-regularized logistic regression (binary classification)
cards.effect: Convergence rates as a function of gradient steps and batch size (magnitudes not specified in abstract)
cards.evidence: Error analysis and convergence rate bounds
cards.quote: We also establish an error analysis for MUON with the generalized NS steps that provides convergence rates in terms of the number of gradient steps and in terms of the size of the mini-batch.
